clinician.final_diagnosis: Echinococcal cyst (hydatid cyst) with daughter cysts in the mediastinum
clinician.trajectory_summary: A 22-year-old man presented with a subacute clinical syndrome of dry cough lasting more than 1 month, chest pain, fatigue, low-grade fever, and night sweats that worsened over the preceding 2 weeks. Physical examination showed normal respiratory and cardiac function. Chest X-ray demonstrated mediastinal enlargement and left pleural effusion. Contrast-enhanced CT (CECT) on admission revealed a 56×50 mm walled cystic mass in the mediastinum in close proximity to the upper left atrium, ascending aorta, and pulmonary artery, with imaging features compatible with hydatid cyst, a 10 mm endoatrial filling defect, left pleural effusion, and upper left lobe consolidation. Serologic testing for echinococcosis (antibody titers) was negative. The cystic mass was confirmed to be an echinococcal cyst containing several daughter cysts measuring up to 10 mm. The patient underwent surgical resection with good postoperative recovery and was discharged 5 days later in good condition. Postoperative medical management consisted of three 28-day courses of albendazole 400 mg twice daily.
